chunk_findings.detail: The change loads bug state twice without a common snapshot: `_unnamed` reads state at line 65, then `_linked` reads it again at line 66. If an open bug is fixed or invalidated between those two reads, `_unnamed` returns `[]` because the failing id already had an open bug, while `_linked` then returns `""` because that bug is gone; the `if not bug and unnamed:` guard is false, so no replacement bug is filed even though the failing test now has no open bug. Concrete interleaving: open bug `B` names test `a`, current run has `ids=[a]`; process A executes `_unnamed` and sees `B` open -> `[]`; a second agent calls `ddflow bug fixed B`; process A then executes `_linked` and sees no open bug -> `""`; no `_file` is made for `a`.

chunk_findings.detail: `_under_resume` locates the insertion point with `text.replace("# ddflow brief", lead + "# ddflow brief", 1)`. This treats the current heading as the first literal substring anywhere in the text, but the RESUME slice is placed before that heading and can itself contain an earlier occurrence, such as a rendered `### ddflow brief` task heading or a recovered prior brief line; in `"## ddflow brief"`/`"### ddflow brief"` the substring `# ddflow brief` occurs starting at the second/third hash. Given that input, the reports/contest/Open-workflow-choices block is inserted inside the RESUME content instead of after it, corrupting the recoverable slice and leaving the new blocks above the rest of the resume work. The insertion point should be a structured marker or a line-anchored match for the current H1 heading rather than the first substring occurrence.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/brief.py:_under_resume

chunk_findings.detail:
`_under_resume` places the reports, contest, and Open-workflow-choices blocks with `text.replace("# ddflow brief", lead + "# ddflow brief", 1)`. That matches the first substring, not the view's heading line. Given a resume slice that itself quotes the brief heading (this repo's recoverable notes and tests do: `"## RESUME
see # ddflow brief
# ddflow brief
## work
"`) plus a non-empty `undecided`, the choices are inserted inside the RESUME section, so the brief no longer opens with recoverable work and the section structure is broken. A resume body with no exact `# ddflow brief` substring drops `reports_block`, `contest_text`, and `undecided` entirely (`if lead else text` never runs when `lead` is non-empty and `replace` finds nothing), so an undecided flow knob disappears instead of moving under the slice.

chunk_findings.detail: `_dedup` can return a bug that does not name every id, yet the caller uses it as the bug for the entire failing set. Given open bug A `"a fails on main"` and open bug B `"b fails on main"`, `_dedup(repo, agent, [a, b])` reaches the fallback `return next(b.id for b in open_bugs if _names(b.summary, ids[0])), unnamed` and returns bug A. The gate path then sets `found["bug"]` to bug A and computes `BR.reason_text([a, b], bug)`, so the run’s reason links both failures to a bug that only names `a`; the actual bug B is not linked from this run. That is wrong for any consumer that reads `found["bug"]` as the bug for the whole failing set.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gate_baseline.py:_dedup
